release.label: Enrolled learner release - clean baseline verified

steps.title: Understand the cache HA system
steps.workplace_problem: A demo service depends on a Redis cache. One cache node is a single point of failure; you need a replica plus an automatic failover coordinator.
learning_outcomes: Why a single cache node is a SPOF
How a replica keeps a warm copy of the data
How a coordinator (sentinel) promotes the replica on failure
steps.architecture: Two cache nodes (cache-1 primary, cache-2 replica) and one coordinator (coordinator-1) running sentinel that monitors both and promotes the replica if the primary dies.
boundaries: The claim is cache-tier availability for a demo service.
The single coordinator-1 node is itself a single point of failure in this demo profile.
A healthy cache alone does not prove the demo service still reads and writes.
steps.opening_prompt: Ask me anything about Redis replication, the coordinator, or how a failover plays out. When it clicks, say start BUILD.
steps.checkpoint: Explain in one sentence what promotes the replica when the primary dies.

steps.title: Install Redis on the primary cache
steps.why: cache-1 is the primary cache node; it needs the Redis server package.
steps.command_explanation: dnf install -y installs the Redis server and its dependencies without prompting.

steps.title: Install Redis on the replica cache
steps.why: cache-2 will hold a warm replica of the primary's data, so it also needs Redis.
steps.command_explanation: The same install on cache-2; each node runs its own Redis server.

steps.title: Make cache-2 a replica of cache-1
steps.why: The replica must follow the primary so it holds a current copy ready to promote.
steps.command_explanation: redis-cli replicaof tells this node to replicate from cache-1 on port 6379.

steps.title: Start and enable Redis on the primary
steps.why: The Redis service must be running and set to start on boot.
steps.command_explanation: systemctl enable --now starts Redis immediately and enables it at boot.
steps.expected: The command returns to the prompt; redis is active.

steps.title: Configure the failover coordinator
steps.why: Sentinel watches the primary and automatically promotes the replica if it fails.
steps.command_explanation: redis-sentinel starts the coordinator using the config that monitors cache-1 and its replica.
steps.expected: Sentinel starts and begins monitoring the cache tier.

steps.title: Verify the cache tier is failover-ready
steps.why: Prove sentinel sees one master and one healthy replica before trusting failover.
steps.command_explanation: Asks sentinel for the master's status; it reports the master and the number of healthy replicas.

steps.title: Write to the primary and read from the replica
steps.why: Confirm data written to the primary is visible on the replica.
steps.command_explanation: Writes a key on the primary; you then read it back from cache-2 to see replication.
steps.expected: OK, and the key is readable on cache-2.

survive.guide: Kill the primary and watch sentinel promote the replica.

landing.title: Operate and recover the cache tier
landing.why: The guided build is complete; use the role terminals to inspect and recover the cache tier.
landing.expected: Sentinel reports the current master and healthy replica count.

scenarios.title: Primary cache failure
scenarios.recover: sentinel promotes cache-2; confirm the new master serves reads and writes
